description: Configure Cursor Agent Mode with .cursor/rules/*.mdc frontmatter (alwaysApply, globs, description), User Rules for AI & safe autonomous diff boundaries.
h1: Cursor Agent Mode and .cursor/rules/*.mdc: frontmatter, globs, and personality rules.
dek: Stop Cursor Agent from making unrequested refactors or writing essay summaries—configure alwaysApply, glob-scoped .mdc rules, and User Rules cleanly.
lede: Cursor’s Agent Mode can edit multiple files, run terminal commands, and iterate on test failures autonomously. Without crisp rules in .cursor/rules/*.mdc and Settings → Rules for AI, autonomous runs tend to touch unrelated files, add unwanted dependencies, or pad diffs with chatty recaps. Here is the exact .mdc frontmatter spec plus an interactive builder.
answer: Put repo-wide Agent Mode guardrails (testing gates, git boundaries, stack conventions) in .cursor/rules/*.mdc using YAML frontmatter—alwaysApply: true for universal rules, globs for file-type rules, or description-only for agent-requested rules. Put your personal communication style (diff-first replies, terse prose, pushback) in Cursor Settings → Rules for AI so you never pollute team git history.

sections.h2: Three battle-tested .cursor/rules/*.mdc templates for Agent Mode.
sections.html:
1. Safe Autonomous Execution (.cursor/rules/agent-guardrails.mdc)

--- description: Safe diff boundaries and verification checks for Cursor Agent Mode alwaysApply: true --- - Keep diffs tightly scoped to the requested task; never refactor unrelated files. - Before installing any new package or changing a database schema, stop and ask. - Run the relevant unit test or build command after your final edit and cite the exact pass/fail result. - Summarize changes in one line per modified file; skip conversational intros and closing offers.

2. Glob-Scoped Backend Route Rules (.cursor/rules/api-routes.mdc)

--- description: Backend API boundary validation and error handling globs: ["src/api/**/*.ts", "app/api/**/*.ts"] alwaysApply: false --- - Validate every request body and query param with Zod at the route boundary. - Return structured JSON error objects with explicit HTTP status codes—never raw stack traces. - Add a regression test for every bug fix in the sibling *.test.ts file.

3. User-Global Personal Tone (Cursor Settings → Rules for AI)

- Lead with the root cause and fix before background narration. - Challenge flawed premises or simpler standard-library alternatives before writing code. - Flag unverified assumptions or skipped checks on their own line instead of smoothing over them.

Using Cursor alongside Claude Code, Codex CLI, Windsurf, or Cline? See our 7-agent coding rules matrix so your repo stays synced via one root AGENTS.md.

faq.a: Yes. Modular .cursor/rules/*.mdc files let you separate always-on guardrails from glob-scoped language or directory rules so you don't waste context window tokens on irrelevant instructions.

faq.q: Does Cursor Agent Mode read AGENTS.md too?
faq.a: Yes. Modern Cursor versions support root AGENTS.md files alongside .cursor/rules/*.mdc, making AGENTS.md an ideal shared baseline for teams mixing Cursor, Codex CLI, and Claude Code.

faq.q: Where do I put personal Cursor communication preferences without committing them to git?
faq.a: Paste personal tone, brevity, and pushback rules into Cursor Settings → Rules for AI (user-level), or add .cursor/rules/personal-*.mdc to your local .git/info/exclude file.

faq.q: How do I stop Cursor Agent Mode from rewriting working code outside my task?
faq.a: Add an alwaysApply: true guardrail rule: 'Keep edits tightly scoped to the requested bug or feature; never refactor or reformat unrelated files unless explicitly asked.'
